channel.title: Moodeng Blog
channel.description: Notes on fair small-loan credit, borrower-owned trust, and building a credit record from zero.

item.title: How to borrow money online in the Philippines without a bank account
item.description: A plain guide to borrowing money online in the Philippines without a bank account: what you need instead of a bank, how funding and repayment work, how to cash out to pesos, and how to avoid predatory loan apps.

item.title: What is a peer-to-peer loan, and is it safe?
item.description: A clear explanation of peer-to-peer (P2P) loans: how they work, how they differ from banks and loan apps, where the real risks sit for borrowers and lenders, and what to check before you borrow or lend.

item.title: How to build credit when you have no credit history
item.description: A practical guide to building credit from zero: why the cold-start problem exists, how to start with small on-time loans, how to make your repayment record portable, and what to avoid.

item.title: Loan sharks didn’t begin with apps
item.description: A history of loan sharking, salary buying, payday lending, and app-based debt collection shows how predatory credit keeps finding the same pressure points.

item.title: Contact-list collateral and the shame tax
item.description: How contact-list access turns small loans into shame pressure, and why fair digital credit should not use borrower contacts as collateral.

item.title: Borrower context should feel like a work rhythm, not a confession
item.description: What lenders need to understand a small loan request, and how borrowers can share payday fit, work rhythm, and purpose without oversharing.

item.title: $15 loans are infrastructure, not a gimmick
item.description: Small USDC loans can matter when the missing infrastructure is identity, settlement, clear terms, and borrower-owned repayment history.

item.title: What oil pipelines teach us about credit
item.description: A book review connecting oil pipeline infrastructure to credit access, loan sharks, and why small loans need borrower-owned records.

item.title: Secret societies and the need for safe trust
item.description: A book review on secret societies, mutual aid, rotating credit, and what fair P2P lending can learn about safe trust.

item.title: What credit risk books miss about loan sharks
item.description: A book review on credit portfolio risk and money theory, with a borrower-side lens on loan sharks and concentrated credit options.

item.title: Your first credit record should not belong to a loan shark
item.description: Why the first credit record should belong to the borrower, not an unregistered loan app using contact-list pressure and fake-looking credibility signals.
